title: One-time passwords for an enrolled device

prose.text: Each enrolled device has a set of one-time passwords an admin can hand a user in place of the app profile's passwords. One API call returns the whole set for one device.

prose.label: The call.
prose.text: What the call returns, and that each OTP is single-use: [[zcc.api.devices-wire:otp]]. {{otp-field-mapping}} What `zdpDisableOtp` unlocks is open {{gap:zdp-otp-meaning}}, and so is how the generic `otp` relates to the rest {{gap:generic-otp-relationship}}. {{anti-tempering-spelling}}

checks.do: Which OTP the user's action needs (logout, exit, uninstall, revert, a service disable, anti-tampering), and whether the device's platform and Client Connector version show OTPs at all.
Whether the OTP was already used, since each one works once.
For a Go caller, whether an empty string means the field was absent rather than an empty password.

otp-meanings.statement: On Client Connector 4.0 and later for Windows, 4.1 and later for macOS and 4.2.1 and later for Linux, the device details page shows OTPs that can be used in place of app profile passwords: Logout, Revert, Uninstall, Exit (exit from the tray without disabling Internet & SaaS), Disable ZIA, Disable ZPA, Disable ZDX, Deception Settings (disables Deception; Windows 4.0 and later), Disable Anti-Tampering (Windows 4.1 and later) and Disable Endpoint DLP (Windows 4.3 and later, macOS 4.2 and later).

quotes: For Zscaler Client Connector version 4.0 and later for Windows, Zscaler Client Connector version 4.1 and later for macOS, and Zscaler Client Connector version 4.2.1 and later for Linux, you can view and copy the following one-time passwords (OTPs) for each enrolled device.
You can use these passwords in place of passwords defined in app profiles.
Revert OTP: The password users must enter to revert to the previous Zscaler Client Connector version.
Exit OTP: The password that users can enter to exit the app from the system tray without disabling Internet & SaaS.
Deception Settings OTP: The password users must enter to disable the Deception service. Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.0 and later for Windows.
Disable Anti-Tampering OTP: The password used to disable anti-tampering protection. Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.1 and later for Windows.
Disable Endpoint DLP OTP: The password users must enter to disable data protection in Zscaler Client Connector.
Logout OTP: The password users must enter to log out of Zscaler Client Connector.
Uninstall OTP: The password users must enter to uninstall Zscaler Client Connector.
Disable ZIA OTP: The password users must enter to disable the Internet & SaaS service.
Disable ZPA OTP: The password users must enter to disable the Private Access service.
Disable ZDX OTP: The password users must enter to disable the ZDX service.
Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.3 and later for Windows and Zscaler Client Connector version 4.2 and later for macOS.

console-one-time-password.statement: The same page also shows a One-Time Password described as a temporary password for login.

quotes: One-Time Password: Displays a temporary password for login.

console-refresh.statement: The passwords on the device details page refresh automatically every 60 minutes while the window is open, and Refresh Status refreshes them on demand.

quotes: Refresh Status: Click this option to refresh the passwords manually to ensure you have the latest password to provide to an end user.
Passwords refresh automatically every 60 minutes while the window is open.

otp-field-mapping.statement: By name, the response's `logoutOtp`, `revertOtp`, `uninstallOtp`, `exitOtp`, `ziaDisableOtp`, `zpaDisableOtp`, `zdxDisableOtp`, `deceptionSettingsOtp` and `antiTemperingDisableOtp` are the portal's Logout, Revert, Uninstall, Exit, Disable ZIA, Disable ZPA, Disable ZDX, Deception Settings and Disable Anti-Tampering OTPs.
otp-field-mapping.conditions: Matched by name between the API contract's eleven response keys and the portal's OTP list; neither source states the mapping.

anti-tempering-spelling.statement: The anti-tampering OTP's key is spelled `antiTemperingDisableOtp` ("Tempering") in the contract and in both SDKs.

otp-expiry.title: How long an unused one-time password stays valid
otp-expiry.detail: The contract says each OTP is single-use; the MCP tool calls them short-lived; the portal refreshes its view hourly. No source gives an expiry, and neither SDK model carries a TTL or expiry field.
otp-expiry.blocks: telling a user whether an OTP fetched earlier still works

zdp-otp-meaning.title: What `zdpDisableOtp` disables
zdp-otp-meaning.detail: By elimination against the portal's list, `zdpDisableOtp` would be the Disable Endpoint DLP OTP, since Deception has its own `deceptionSettingsOtp`; but the password contract describes `zdpDisablePass` as the password to disable Zscaler Deception. The device-detail prefixes have the same open question (zcc.devices.record-fields, gap zd-vs-zdp). On one recorded macOS device the `getOtp` response has `zdpDisableOtp` but no `deceptionSettingsOtp` (claim recorded-otp-subset), and the portal gives the Deception Settings OTP for Windows only; this fits the Endpoint DLP reading but does not settle it.
zdp-otp-meaning.blocks: handing a user the right OTP to disable Endpoint DLP or Deception

generic-otp-relationship.title: How the generic `otp` relates to the operation OTPs
generic-otp-relationship.detail: The portal describes One-Time Password as a temporary password for login, separate from the operation OTPs; whether the API's `otp` is that value, and whether it unlocks any of the operations, is not stated. The legacy example returns only `otp`, while one recorded OneAPI response omits it and returns eight operation OTPs (claims doc-example-otp-only, recorded-otp-subset).
generic-otp-relationship.blocks: knowing whether one OTP can stand in for the others
